His clock was verified correct, so the fast gallery clock cannot rescue him. The false late location overlaps the glass's 6:40 delivery and 6:46 pour, and he admits business around the salon beforehand. Other late claimants know the real installation; other cabinet claimants give early times. Hugh is the unique intersection. Shared key/linen access prevents treating conservation or Monet's access as a shortcut. I would ask Hugh to point to his imaginary brass post and explain how he crossed a locked curtain.

confusing_mechanics: The briefing tells me I am innocent but gives me an objectively impossible 6:44 alcove claim without any private explanation for why I said it. As a direct-questioning actor I cannot honestly answer the obvious follow-up about my own whereabouts.

Many guests have false alcove claims, yet stage 3 explains their unrelated scandals rather than those false claims. Unique double inconsistency is a strong puzzle answer, but one falsehood versus two is not logically proof of who poisoned the glass.
The wording switches among enclosure, cabinet and alcove; the photographs clarify the cabinet, but the actual installation photo does not show the enclosing security curtain.
repetition: Six late guests repeat 'My other business that evening is not something I wanted Grant announcing over dinner'; six early obsolete-cabinet visitors repeat the same outside-enclosure sentence. The regular matrix makes testimony feel engineered and signals the sorting rule. Stage 3 largely repeats grievances then says they concern something else.
giveaways: Late Hugh is the sole obsolete-feature claimant in that time group, and his 'salon before that' sentence alone draws attention to the poison location. The emphatic PROPOSAL / NOT AN INSTALLATION RECORD and correct clock checks make the two-axis solution easy once F4 arrives. The visuals themselves are strong, readable evidence.
improvements: Give each innocent with a false time or obsolete description a private, playable explanation so interrogation can resolve their claim without inventing facts.
Vary the repeated testimony structure and make the other-business hints natural to each role.
Add one discriminating salon or coupe fact connecting Hugh to contamination, so the final case goes beyond the unique double liar.
Keep both independent records and clock correction: they reward comparison instead of motive guessing.
limitations: Asynchronous scripted reading, not real party timing. Viewed all three required images and only this player's staged materials. No live questioning, other private briefings, organizer information or solution read. Confidence describes the intended inference from supplied evidence, not independently proven guilt. Stage 1 and stage 2 judgments were saved before reading subsequent stages.
